term: degree of existence, world-relative presence and necessary being
resolution: ExistenceDegrees uses intensity as an ordered degree parameter and m.ExistsAt as a separate world-relative presence predicate over a fixed roster. NecessaryAt is relative to worlds accessible from the chosen standpoint and need not imply base-world presence without a reflexivity/presence premise. Neither presence nor necessity alone fixes intensity; the degree-invariance clause is an additional open, source-shaped conditional. The source11 claim binds only ActualNecessaryDegreeInvariant, whose antecedent includes actual presence and necessity, not the stronger bare analyst predicate. Same degree means mutual≤, allowing different tied labels; no source-supported equality of labels, strictness or uniqueness is inferred. The graded-intensity profile is not silently identified with Thomistic InAct x esse, the earlier homogeneous MoreIn scale, or a count of worlds. All global conclusions retain their root-accessible domain and existent-pair guards.
